claim: It's a perfect time of year for cold exposure: for a lot of listeners, though not everywhere, it's getting into the coldest part of the year
Even a little cold exposure has powerful physical, mental health and "drive to get shit done" benefits
There are a lot of studies on cold exposure, and you can look up the science, on boosting the immune system and so on
Personally, one of the two biggest benefits of cold exposure is a huge mental reset and mental-emotional lift
Personally, nothing ever found is really as powerful as cold exposure at shifting your state, other than maybe breath work, really amazing too but at times kind of more work to get started
Personally, cold snaps us out of repetitive down kind of states
Personally, one of the two biggest benefits of cold exposure is that it gets us in touch with willpower: stepping into a little discomfort because it leads where I want to go
Stepping into a little discomfort because it leads where I want to go is the same fundamental choice we need to make throughout the day to create the life we want
Personally, cold showers are so effective for getting into the frame of mind of willpower, stepping into a little discomfort because it leads where I want to go
A way to get cold exposure: start your day with a cold shower
A way to get cold exposure: work out outside, or go to work and the store, in less clothes than you otherwise would
For cold exposure, you don't need to always have a jacket on if it's cold: wear a t-shirt
The cold engine: we have a cold engine, brown fat, trained basically the way a few push-ups dropped into the day train muscles

Every little bit of cold trains the cold engine, brown fat: a 30-second or 10-minute cold shower, an ice bath, shoveling your driveway in a t-shirt, walking from the car to work in a short-sleeve shirt
The cold engine, brown fat, helps keep you warm and adapt to cold
Cold showers are one of the fundamental habits heard over and over, from men worked with in coaching, talked to or listening to the show, as one that sticks
To make cold showers stick, get over the hump: do it every day for a couple of weeks, three weeks, notice how much different you feel, and it sticks
Personally, so many men come to mind who can't imagine going back from cold showers, because cold showers can shift your mind, emotions and body: "It's so worth it, I promise"
Fascia is basically a wrapper, almost a fabric, around our entire body
Tightness around a muscle after a workout is, in general, fascia tightness
Fascia tightness sometimes becomes a trigger point, a stuck spot you've felt if you train regularly: a bunching up where energy can't really flow and gets sort of stuck and stagnant

Emotional trigger points: the same bunching up as a fascia trigger point, where energy can't really flow and gets stuck, happens with emotions, because emotions are a physical thing that lives in our body
Unlike our mind, the body never ever forgets
A two-year-old's trauma might still impact them 20, 40 or 60 years later, not because the mind remembers but because the body does
From childhood on, experiences often create some kind of trauma
Trauma is really just emotional energy, especially energy we can't process at the time, and it becomes stuck as a physical thing
"Triggered" is kind of a common word today

When a message or conversation triggers you and you suddenly feel completely different, mentally and a lot of times physically, what really happens is that it triggers the physical stuckness of that emotion
When we really heal something and completely move past it, we keep the memory but it loses its energetic charge, so it no longer brings up the emotions
The energetic charge of a memory that brings up emotions is a physical thing
Stuck, stagnant emotional energy can be released
One method to release stuck emotional energy, encouraged as something to try: enter your body and find the emotional trigger as a physical thing

To release an emotional trigger, say a text from your wife snaps you into anger, frustration, sadness, guilt or shame, and you feel it in your body. Suggested: search for it as a physical sensation and identify with it as one
What seems to happen with a lot of stuck emotional energy is that we lose the physical connection to it

What seems to happen with a lot of stuck emotional energy: a breakup, say, triggers you, fades, then comes back a day, a week or a month later, again and again, because we lose the physical connection with that stuck energy, and so it kind of hides in the body
It seems that, however much we think or talk through a stuck emotion, if we don't physically reconnect with that emotional energy in the body, it stays stuck

Finding emotions as physical sensations is used in a type of therapy called somatic experiencing, which basically takes people through identifying emotions and experiences with their physical sensations
In somatic experiencing, identifying with emotions and experiences as physical sensations is what lets the charge be released
Releasing emotional triggers by finding them as physical sensations, as in somatic experiencing, is a really simple but really powerful method
Step one to release an emotional trigger, as in somatic experiencing: recognize when you're being triggered
Without meditating, without the awareness to step back and observe your thoughts, you won't really recognize when you're being triggered, just be swept up
With a regular meditation practice you may notice being triggered in the moment
Step two to release an emotional trigger, as in somatic experiencing: enter the body, bringing your awareness into its physical sensations, a phrase that means more if you've meditated
To enter the body, start by closing your eyes and feeling the weight of your body, your feet on the ground, your legs on the chair
The breath is a great gateway into the body's sensations
name: Breathing

claim: Step three to release an emotional trigger, as in somatic experiencing: identify the trigger as a physical thing
Sometimes an emotional trigger is in a particular part of the body, because certain trauma gets stored in a particular part
An emotional trigger may be generalized, almost cellular: then identify the nature of the feeling. Is it warm? What does it feel like?
To identify an emotional trigger as a physical thing, let go of the thought side and connect to the physical thing
Releasing emotional triggers by finding them in the body was an introduction, maybe for more depth at a future time
When something triggers you, sit, close your eyes, enter your body and really dive in

To find emotions in the body: in the 1987 movie Inner Space, which some listeners weren't alive for, Dennis Quaid was shrunk into basically a little spaceship and injected into Martin Short. Suggested: almost imagine you're in that microscopic ship, venturing around your body. Can you find those emotions? Where are they? What do they feel like?
Connecting to emotions physically can really release their charge
Experiment with finding emotions in your body and connecting to them physically
We all have stuff that triggers us emotionally, because we're all human beings
